record.paper_title: An Open Problem on Sparse Representations in Unions of Bases
record.original_question: Let D be a dictionary formed as a union of q + 1 orthonormal bases, with q at least 2. Let the spark eta(D) be the smallest number of columns of D that are linearly dependent, and let the mutual coherence mu(D) be the largest absolute normalized inner product between distinct columns of D. Two known lower bounds relate spark to mutual coherence: for an arbitrary dictionary, eta(D) >= 1 + 1/mu(D), and for a union of q + 1 orthonormal bases, eta(D) >= (1 + 1/q) / mu(D). Are these lower bounds tight for dictionaries that are unions of several orthonormal bases, in the sense that one can construct such dictionaries where the corresponding lower-bound value is actually achieved?

evidence.quote: Motivated by these open questions, we study the tightness of the estimate (I.1) and the estimate (I.3).
Our results imply that two well-known estimates for the spark are indeed tight.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times N}$ (or $\mathbb{C}^{n\times N}$) be a dictionary obtained as the concatenation of $q+1$ orthonormal bases of the underlying $n$-dimensional Hilbert space, where $q\ge 2$. Denote the (unit-norm) columns of $D$ by $d_1,\dots,d_N$. Define:
- the spark $\eta(D)$ as the smallest cardinality of a set of columns of $D$ that are linearly dependent;
- the mutual coherence $\mu(D)=\max_{i\ne j}\,|\langle d_i,d_j\rangle|$.

It is known that for any dictionary with unit-norm columns
$$\eta(D)\ \ge\ 1+\frac{1}{\mu(D)},\qquad(\ast)$$
and that for a dictionary $D$ formed as a union of $q+1$ orthonormal bases
$$\eta(D)\ \ge\ \frac{1+1/q}{\mu(D)}.\qquad(\ast\ast)$$

Question: Are the bounds $(\ast)$ and $(\ast\ast)$ tight within the class of dictionaries that are unions of orthonormal bases? More precisely, do there exist, for suitable parameters, dictionaries $D$ given as unions of orthonormal bases for which equality is attained in $(\ast)$, and dictionaries $D$ given as unions of $q+1$ orthonormal bases for which equality is attained in $(\ast\ast)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The tightness of both lower bounds has been established constructively. Using families of mutually unbiased bases from quantum information theory, explicit unions of orthonormal bases are constructed that attain equality in each of the two bounds, resolving the question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: An Open Problem on Sparse Representations in Unions of Bases
status_evidence.snippet: We constructively prove that both of them are tight... using a family of mutually unbiased bases which first appears in quantum information theory.
status_evidence.claim: Both spark-vs-coherence lower bounds are shown to be tight via explicit constructions based on mutually unbiased bases.
